prompt: A tent forms an isosceles triangle with the ground. Each base angle — where a wall meets the ground — measures $52^\circ$. What is the measure, in degrees, of the vertex angle at the peak?
hint: An isosceles triangle has two equal base angles. Think about how much of the triangle's angle total they use together.

hints.text: An isosceles triangle has two equal base angles. Think about how much of the triangle's angle total they use together.
The two base angles total $2 \times 52 = 104^\circ$. Subtract that from the $180^\circ$ in a triangle to get the peak angle.
$180 - 104 = 76$, so the vertex angle at the peak is $76^\circ$.

explanation: The tent is an isosceles triangle, so its two base angles are congruent and each one is $52^\circ$.
Together the base angles take up $2 \times 52 = 104^\circ$ of the triangle.
The three angles total $180^\circ$, so the vertex angle is $180 - 104 = 76^\circ$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Sanity-check the shape
steps: A $76^\circ$ peak is wider than each $52^\circ$ base angle, so the tent is a bit squat — that matches a tent with a broad base.
